flagged.topic: Amana insert V-groove v16, 1-flute ramp column
flagged.finding: The reading is right. I read all 36 rows. Every 1-flute row from 40 to 110 deg (RC-1040 to RC-1105, 24 rows) prints Ramp Down = Feed/2 in all six materials (40/20, 90/45, 80/40). Only RC-1146 (120 deg) and RC-1101 (150 deg), both at 14,000 RPM, print Ramp = Feed (90/90, 180/180). Every 2-flute row prints Feed/2. The footer rule 'Feed Rate IPM / # of Flutes' gives 1.0 for 1 flute. So the printed 1-flute column fraction is 0.5, and the rule is not followed. Extra: the 1-flute 18,000 RPM rows agree with their chip load (18,000 x 1 x .0024 = 43 IPM, printed 40). RC-1146 and RC-1101 do not (14,000 x 1 x .0024 = 33.6, printed 90); these two rows look like copied 2-flute rows. ToolsToday prints RC-1108 as 30 -> 15, the same 0.5.

Not defined. I searched the 33 Amana text files under fetch/G*/sources and the 6 G10 Amana PDFs. 'Ramp' occurs only as the column header 'Ramp Down' and the rule 'To find Ramp Down: Feed Rate IPM / # of flutes' (MPM on the metric page of Spektra v27). 'Plunge' occurs only in product names. amanatool.com HTML pages (knowledge_base, router-bit-technical-information) return 403. The only reading in text is the distributor ToolsToday: 'ramp-down or plunge rate'. The current Spektra chart v27 prints the same rows as v24.

flagged.topic: IDC plunge column and spiral drilling footnote
flagged.finding: Confirmed from PDF p14-p19 (section 2) and p11 (starter set). All 14 fractions recompute. The asterisk sits only on the Plunge cell '60*' of the 'Drilling' row of the 1/8 in DRILLING ENDMILL table (PDF p11); the 'Conventional' row (Plunge 25) has no asterisk. So the footnote 'The plunge value is for using the spiral drilling technique' covers that one cell only. Two table conflicts: 60 deg V-bit 60/20 (section 2) against 40/20 (starter set), and 90 deg V-bit 45/25 against 50/25; the fetch notes give only the first. A separate asterisk on the starter-set 1/8 in ballnose step-over '40%*' has no footnote on that page.

flagged.topic: SGS End Mill Matrix row mapping
flagged.finding: Confirmed. I rendered PDF p7 and p8 (catalogue pp. 22-23). They are a two-page spread with 26 rows each, at the same vertical positions (for example Series 33 and the first value row are both at the top line; Down Cut Router and the last value row are both at the bottom). The order mapping is therefore also a position mapping. Every ramp value in the statements is right: Series 7 = 1, Z5 = 7, H-Carb 77 = 1, Multi Carb 66 = 1, Turbo Carb 56B = 25, S-Carb 47 = 90, S-Carb 43 = 90, 20-CCR and 31-CCR = 'Based upon end style' / '5 (for end cut styles)', Compression Router 25 = 5, Up Cut Router 21 = 90, Down Cut Router 22 = '–'. The Center Cutting column is also right for each. For the other rows: Series 33 90, Z1 90, Z1P 90, ZH1 20, V-Carb 5, T-Carb 3, ZD1 2, Power-Carb 1, Ski-Carb 90, 43CB 90, APR-3 90, APR-4 90, APF 25, Slow Helix 5. The Z1 and Z1P rows look plausible to me (R,B and S,R,B), but the part did not use them, so no statement depends on them. Z5 conflict: confirmed. The matrix prints 7 deg; the Z5 chart (PDF p19, catalogue p34) prints 'ramp up to 5 degrees using slotting speed and feed rates. Do not plunge.' The catalogue gives no reason for the difference. The dash for Down Cut Router has no legend. Missed data: the colour code is readable in the image. Compression, Up Cut and Down Cut Router, CCR and Slow Helix are coded only 'Non Ferrous N5 to N7'. The legend also marks 'Plunging not recommended in these materials' for Stainless M1-M3, High Temp S1-S3, Titanium S4 and Hardened H1-H4. It gives no plunge mark for N1-N7. The part has no statement for this legend.

flagged.topic: IMCO helical bore formula and helix angles
flagged.finding: Confirmed from PDF p1 (printed p130): 'The diameter of the starting hole will be: (tool diameter x 2) - (corner radius x 2)'. Angles: IPT/C 7, 9, 11, 13 = 0.5 deg; APT/C 5 = 3 deg; M525, M527, M503, M726, M706, M806, M924, M904, M905, E14, E13, E12, M104 = 1-2.5 deg; M223, M233, M203, M202 = 3-5 deg. Feed: IPT/C and APT/C 'IPT or MMPT x 1.6' (high-pressure coolant) and 'x 1.25' (flood); M and E series 'Slotting feed in chart'. Step 2 (p131): 3xD for IPT/C 7, 9 and 3.75xD for 11, 13. Method B uses 1.6 and 0.5 deg for 9, 11, 13. Internal conflict: Method A lists IPT/C 7 for a second step, but the text says seven or fewer flutes need one step. No material is printed per series.

The documents do not define it. Exact sentences: (1) types-tool-entry blog: 'Helical Interpolation is a very common and safe practice of tool entry with ferrous materials. Employing corner radius end mills during this operation will decrease tool wear and lessen corner breakdown. With this method, use a programmed helix diameter of greater than 110-120% of the cutter diameter.' (2) Helical guidebook 2016 p4, visible layer: 'We recommend a programmed helix diameter >110-120% of tool diameter.' The word 'programmed' suggests the CAM helix setting, but CAM systems use this word for both the bore and the path, so the text does not decide it. The part's two derived readings (path 0.1-0.2 D if bore; bore 2.1-2.2 D if path) recompute correctly.

Confirmed. I rendered p4 and p5. The visible layer prints: 'Employing corner radius end mills during this operation will decrease tool wear', 'We recommend a programmed helix diameter >110-120% of tool diameter', 'Soft/Non-Ferrous Materials: 3° – 10°', 'Hard/Ferrous Materials: 1° – 3°' (p4); 'The tool must be center cutting', 'the feed rate upon entry is recommended to be reduced by at least 50%', 'The feed rate in this scenario should be reduced by 50%' (p5). All quoted numbers are in the visible layer. The hidden layers carry 'increase tool wear', 'must be reduced by at least 50%' and 'Non-Ferrous / Ferrous' labels with the same numbers. The SGS PDF p9 also carries 3-4 text layers of the Entry Methods block; all layers give the same numbers.

Not found in a primary source. The Burnette page (a reseller) prints: 'For deep pockets where axial depth exceeds 1.5 times the tool diameter, reduce the chip load by 25% and utilize a ramp-in entry angle of no more than 10° to mitigate vertical plunge stresses.' It cites no Amana document. No Amana PDF I checked prints a ramp angle; amanatool.com HTML pages return 403. The refusal to store it is right.

Found, but not from Vortex. The text is on https://clebitco.com/speeds-and-feeds/ (Cle Bit Co, a reseller and sharpening shop that sells Vortex and Amana; HTTP 200, fresh copy in verify/a_work/clebitco_speeds_and_feeds.html, sha256 8d4fc3c1...4e77): 'Feeding the the Tool into the material Plunge the material at a 45 DEG angle over 2-4 inches if possible at ⅓ of the calculated feed rate.' It follows a paragraph about the Vortex #3420 compression bit, which explains the misattribution. The Vortex catalogue does not contain it. At most grade c reseller advice; it must not be cited as Vortex.
